def: The most abundant liver and gut drug-metabolizing enzyme, handling about half of all drugs. Inhibitors (ketoconazole, grapefruit juice) raise drug levels; inducers (rifampin) lower them.
A Staphylococcus aureus superantigen that crosslinks MHC II with T-cell receptors, causing massive cytokine release, fever, rash and shock.
A pattern of preoccupation with order, perfectionism and control, without true obsessions or compulsions, and the person sees the traits as appropriate.
Movement side effects of antipsychotics from D2 blockade in the basal ganglia: dystonia, parkinsonism, akathisia and tardive dyskinesia.
A cell adhesion protein (PECAM-1) on endothelial cells and platelets. A marker used to identify vascular tumors such as angiosarcoma.
A B-cell surface receptor (CD21) that binds complement fragments and is also the receptor for Epstein-Barr virus.
Also called Fas, a death receptor that triggers apoptosis when bound by Fas ligand.
NK cells bind the Fc region of IgG-coated target cells via CD16 and kill them with perforin and granzymes.
A hemidesmosome protein in the epidermal basement membrane; its autoantibodies cause bullous pemphigoid.
Conserved microbial structures, such as LPS and flagellin, recognized by innate immune receptors like Toll-like receptors.
Innate immune receptors recognizing pathogen-associated molecular patterns. Activation signals through NF-kB to induce inflammatory cytokines.
Somatic rearrangement of variable, diversity and joining gene segments creating diverse antibody and T-cell receptor genes, mediated by RAG1 and RAG2.
RAG1 and RAG2 encode enzymes that cut DNA for V(D)J recombination in developing lymphocytes. Mutations cause severe combined immunodeficiency.
A B-cell signaling enzyme needed for B-cell maturation, mutated in X-linked agammaglobulinemia.
A BTK mutation causes absent B cells and very low immunoglobulins of all classes, so boys get recurrent bacterial infections after maternal IgG wanes.
Also called La; autoantibodies against it occur in Sjogren syndrome and neonatal lupus.
Zinc-dependent enzymes degrading extracellular matrix in tissue remodeling, wound healing and cancer invasion.
A receptor tyrosine kinase inhibiting growth of cartilage. Activating mutations cause achondroplasia.
Cytokines produced by leukocytes that signal between immune cells.
Inflammatory pain and morning stiffness in the shoulder and hip girdles in older adults, with high ESR and rapid steroid response. Linked with giant cell arteritis.
The intracellular binding partner of tacrolimus, forming a complex that inhibits calcineurin.
New cases per unit of person-time at risk, a measure of the instantaneous rate of disease occurrence.
Enzymes that drive the cell cycle when bound to cyclins. Inhibited by p21 and p16.
Proximal tubule transporters that secrete drugs and organic anions, such as penicillin and methotrexate, into urine.
Failure of leg vein valves with venous pooling, causing edema, varicose veins, skin discoloration and ulcers.
A sugar that alternates with N-acetylglucosamine in the backbone of bacterial peptidoglycan.
An endotoxin of Neisseria and Haemophilus lacking the O antigen of lipopolysaccharide.
Hormone chain from CRH to ACTH to cortisol, regulated by negative feedback.
Enzymes in gram-negative bacteria that hydrolyze penicillins and cephalosporins; carbapenems are used for treatment.
A graph of sensitivity against 1-specificity across test cutoffs; area under the curve measures test discrimination.
An enzyme in a signaling cascade that phosphorylates MAP kinase. Anthrax lethal factor cleaves it.
Basic self-care tasks such as bathing, dressing, eating and toileting; dependence on them distinguishes dementia from normal aging.
A psychotherapy for PTSD that uses guided eye movements while recalling trauma.
A drug that binds acrolein in the bladder, preventing hemorrhagic cystitis from cyclophosphamide and ifosfamide.
A receptor tyrosine kinase driving angiogenesis, inhibited by sunitinib and sorafenib.
A strain that attaches to intestinal epithelium, effacing microvilli and causing infant diarrhea without toxin.
Oral anticoagulants that directly inhibit factor Xa or thrombin, such as rivaroxaban, apixaban and dabigatran.
CT scan done after intravenous contrast, used to evaluate masses such as pancreatic cancer.
The ankle ligament most often sprained, injured in inversion.
Cell surface proteins mediating neuronal adhesion; rabies virus uses them to enter at the neuromuscular junction.
Illness from hantavirus, spread by rodent excreta, with fever, bleeding and kidney failure.
Mitochondrial inherited painless central vision loss in young men.
A childhood pattern of angry, argumentative, defiant behavior toward authority, without violating others' rights.
Ultrasound and nonstress test scoring fetal well-being by breathing, movement, tone, amniotic fluid and heart-rate reactivity.
Coloboma, heart defects, choanal atresia, growth retardation, genital and ear anomalies, from CHD7 mutation.
A 0 to 10 newborn assessment at 1 and 5 minutes of heart rate, respiration, tone, reflexes and color.
Pain and dysfunction of the jaw joint and chewing muscles.
The percent of skin burned, estimated by the rule of nines and used to calculate fluid resuscitation.
A hormone from ovarian follicles, used to estimate ovarian reserve; also made by fetal Sertoli cells.
A physician order that cardiopulmonary resuscitation not be attempted in cardiac arrest.
Catheter measurement of aldosterone in each adrenal vein to tell unilateral adenoma from bilateral hyperplasia in primary aldosteronism.
Acute middle ear infection with a bulging, red tympanic membrane.
Clinical rules identifying low-risk trauma patients who need no cervical spine imaging.
Bleeding proximal to the ligament of Treitz, with hematemesis or melena.
Alcohol, a CNS depressant metabolized by alcohol dehydrogenase.
Score for streptococcal pharyngitis: fever, tonsillar exudates, tender anterior cervical nodes and absent cough.
The organization publishing stepwise guidelines for asthma management.
Detects viral genetic material, such as HIV RNA, used to confirm infection or detect early infection.
Serum albumin minus ascitic albumin; 1.1 or more indicates portal hypertension.
Surgical removal of both ovaries and fallopian tubes.
Fetal weight below the 10th percentile for gestational age.
Drugs that inhibit cyclooxygenase, reducing prostaglandins.
Moderate dysplasia of the cervical squamous epithelium caused by HPV.
Pills with estrogen and progestin that suppress ovulation.
Large trial of hormone replacement therapy.
Inflammation with granulation tissue plugs in alveoli, formerly bronchiolitis obliterans organizing pneumonia.
Birth weight above the 90th percentile for gestational age.
Early atrial depolarizations producing extra heartbeats.
